lines: The episode argues that local political resistance to data centers is undercutting the AI growth story, forcing investors to rethink the huge capex assumptions that underpin current AI valuations.

Because the AI trade rests on a narrow group of companies that need near-perfect execution, the hosts say even small regulatory or supply-chain hurdles can hit the whole sector, which helps explain recent stock volatility.

They expect Anthropic to press ahead with its IPO to cash in on its recent growth before competition and sheer scale erode its valuation upside, and note claims that AI-assisted research has roughly doubled its pace of model development.
On prediction markets, the view is that they track sentiment in real time but mostly piggyback on existing polling models rather than discovering new information.
The hosts also see a communications crisis for the industry: the physical footprint of data centers has opened a gap between AI's promise and its disruptive local impact.
title: AI Stockpocalypse, Anthropic Nears RSI?, Prediction Markets vs. Pollsters
